title: CLAUDE.md said a source-touching PR fires source-gates twice; the path filter is per-PUSH, so the head commit decides and the handoff built on it would have waited forever
description:
Found while following a predecessor handoff, not by auditing the file.

THE HANDOFF SAID, as step 1 of an ordered list: "gh pr checks 145 -- wait for both source-gates runs (a source-touching PR fires it twice here, pull_request + push; that is correct, not a duplicate)". That instruction is a faithful application of this repository CLAUDE.md profile section, whose heading read "A source-touching PR fires source-gates twice; a .quest/-only one fires it once".

PR #145 touched src/application/agents/guides.ts and a test file, so it is source-touching by that wording. Its head SHA 4374c69 carried ONE source-gates row, and mergeStateStatus was already CLEAN. A successor following the instruction waits forever for a second run that correctly never existed.

THE MECHANISM, measured rather than reasoned. The push trigger in .github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml is path-filtered (src/**, test/**, bin/**, npm/**, scripts/qualification/**, package.json, bun.lock, tsconfig.json, four named scripts) and the filter applies to EACH INDIVIDUAL PUSH, never to the pull request cumulative diff. The pull_request trigger has no path filter at all, which is why exactly one row always appears.

Across the three heads of PR #145:
  200f203  src/ + test/    push run fired      source-gates x2
  cbea37e  test/           push run fired      source-gates x2
  4374c69  .quest/ only    NO push run         source-gates x1, and COMPLETE
Confirmed against the runs API filtered by head_sha: only pull_request events exist for 4374c69, for every workflow, while event=push rows exist for the two earlier heads on the same branch.

So the profile was right about the mechanism and wrong about the UNIT -- it said PR where the trigger says PUSH. The original 2026-09-12 observations (PR #24 twice, PR #22 and #26 once) are all still literally true; they are just three cases where the head commit happened to agree with the cumulative diff, which is the common case and exactly why the wrong unit survived.

SECOND, SMALLER STALENESS in the same section. Its closing bullet named the required checks as "(source-gates, Tracker integrity)". Re-measured against rules/branches/main: there are THREE -- source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check -- which is the set the ruleset paragraph at the TOP of the same profile already records, correctly, dated 2026-09-15. So one file disagreed with itself about the gate, the same defect QCLI-315 just fixed between two guide surfaces of the CLI. Worth stating plainly: the enumeration rule from QCLI-315 was written the same night and did not get applied to the file it was written in.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The profile section states the unit correctly -- the path filter applies per PUSH and the HEAD COMMIT decides whether a second source-gates row exists -- and carries the three-head measurement from PR #145 rather than asserting it
The original 2026-09-12 observations are preserved rather than rewritten, since they remain true; the amendment is additive and dated
The required-checks bullet names all three contexts, re-measured against rules/branches/main, and no longer contradicts the ruleset paragraph earlier in the same file

implementationNotes:
ONE REFINEMENT AFTER THE FIRST FIX, and it is the fleet continuous-improvement rule applied to my own repair.

The amendment explained the per-push mechanism correctly and then closed by telling the reader to confirm with the runs API and read the event field -- i.e. to COUNT source-gates ROWS and decide whether the count is complete. That still requires knowing which of two numbers is right for this particular head commit, which is precisely the judgement that was wrong in the first place. I documented the judgement instead of removing it.

mergeStateStatus is the rollup over the required set and does not care how many rows produced it: UNSTABLE while anything required is pending or failed, CLEAN once the required set is satisfied. It is also what I actually used to decide PR #145 was mergeable -- so the advice I wrote was not even the method I had just followed. The runs API now appears only as a way to EXPLAIN a count, never to decide whether to wait.

Prefer a fix that removes the need for judgement over one that documents the judgement. Landed as fe8670d on the same branch.
finalSummary:
Two stale claims corrected in this repository CLAUDE.md profile, both measured, both found by USING the file rather than auditing it. Landed as PR #147, squash-merged to dev as 74f4aac, with two follow-on amendments in PR #150 (6260be0).

1. THE UNIT WAS WRONG. The heading said a source-touching PR fires source-gates twice. The push trigger path filter applies per PUSH, so the HEAD COMMIT decides. Measured across the three heads of PR #145: 200f203 (src/ + test/) and cbea37e (test/) each fired the push run and carried two rows; 4374c69 (.quest/ only) fired no push run and carried one, with mergeStateStatus already CLEAN. Confirmed against the runs API filtered by head_sha, reading the event field.

2. THE REQUIRED-CHECKS BULLET NAMED TWO CONTEXTS; there are three, re-measured against rules/branches/main. The ruleset paragraph at the top of the same profile already had all three, so the file disagreed with itself -- the QCLI-315 enumeration defect, in the file where that rule had been recorded an hour earlier.

The 2026-09-12 observations are preserved unrewritten. They remain true, and they were three cases where the head commit happened to agree with the cumulative diff -- the common case, and exactly why the wrong unit survived four days.

WHY IT COST SOMETHING RATHER THAN NOTHING: my predecessor handoff said, as step 1 of an ordered list, "wait for both source-gates runs". That was a faithful application of the file. Following it means waiting forever for a run that correctly never existed, on a PR that was already mergeable. A stale profile claim does not fail loudly; it becomes an instruction that stalls the next session, and the session obeying it has no reason to doubt it.

THREE AMENDMENTS AFTER THE FIRST FIX, each because the previous version documented a judgement instead of removing one.
  a. The first version explained the mechanism and then told the reader to confirm by counting source-gates rows -- which still requires knowing which of two numbers is right for this head, i.e. the judgement that was wrong to begin with. Replaced with mergeStateStatus, which is the rollup and was the method I had actually used.
  b. opum-cli-e2e supplied the general form: NEWEST-PER-CONTEXT, of which mergeStateStatus is one correct implementation. Sent after I restated the row-counting belief -- four messages after citing this very correction to them, while holding a merge on PR #149 whose head was already the one-row case. Measured before merging: head fb08648 touches .quest/ and CLAUDE.md, no push run exists, one source-gates row, CLEAN. I would have hung on the PR I wrote the rule about.
  c. The prose/tool mismatch has TWO DIRECTIONS and only one is detectable by reading the sentence. Mine was prose-wrong/tool-right, which fails CLOSED -- my waits were already newest-per-context, so nothing ever hung; only the description counted rows, and the description is what travelled to a peer under their name. Theirs was prose-right/tool-wrong, which fails OPEN. The dangerous pairing is the one where the description is accurate, because that is the one a reviewer signs off on.

VERIFIED throughout: quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude exit 0 on every commit (the edits sit outside the managed markers); lore check 63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0. Also verified against this repository own qualification scripts, which already use the assert-nothing-bad shape rather than a fixed count, so nothing needed changing there -- but that was a measurement, not an assumption.
